subject: drama
intro: Drama leads to the stage and screen professions — performing and directing, writing scripts, designing what the audience sees and hears, and teaching theatre itself.

roles.title: Producers and Directors
roles.what: Produce or direct stage, television, radio, video or film productions, making the creative decisions: interpreting the script, choosing actors, and steering set design, sound and special effects.
roles.where: The From script to performance unit — interpreting a published play from a director's viewpoint — is this job in miniature, and the staging and design unit supplies the vocabulary for the creative choices directors own.

roles.title: Writers and Authors
roles.what: Originate and prepare written material such as scripts, stories and other content, developing dramatic material from an idea through drafts to a workable finished text.
roles.where: Devising original drama from a stimulus trains exactly the skill of building a script from nothing, while the elements of practical drama unit — structure and plot, characterisation, dialogue — teach what a script must carry.

roles.title: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in drama, music and the arts to college students, either primarily teaching or combining teaching with research into their own artistic practice.
roles.where: Every performance skill in the course — vocal and physical techniques, use of space, role creation, rehearsal discipline — becomes material to teach, and the written paper's reflective analysis prefigures the scholarly side of the job.

roles.title: Set and Exhibit Designers
roles.what: Design sets and special exhibits for film, video, television and theatre productions, studying scripts, conferring with directors and researching styles and period detail to create the right environment.
roles.where: The Staging and design unit — costume, set and props, lighting, sound and stage space — is the designer's canvas, and reading published plays for performance teaches what a set must make possible in each scene.

roles.title: Audio and Video Technicians
roles.entry: Postsecondary nondegree award or associate's degree
roles.what: Set up, maintain and dismantle audio and video equipment — microphones, speakers, mixing boards, video cameras and cabling — for live and recorded events, from concerts to conferences.
roles.where: The lighting and sound topics of the Staging and design unit, plus the group performance coursework, give the stage-side understanding of what sound and picture equipment must deliver in front of an audience.
